text: Establish and use the formula ∫ 1 ax+b dx = 1 a ln|ax + b| + C, where a and b are constants and a ≠0

text: Establish and use indefinite integrals of the form ∫f(ax + b)dx, where a and b are constants and a ≠0, and f(x)= sin x, f(x)= cos x and f(x)= sec2 x
tex: Establish and use indefinite integrals of the form $\int f(ax+b)\,dx$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants and $a\ne 0$, and $f(x)=\sin x$, $f(x)=\cos x$ and $f(x)=\sec^2 x$

text: Describe, in the case where f(x)≥0 for all values of x in the interval a ≤x ≤b, the area bounded by the graph of the continuous function y = f(x), the x-axis and the lines x = a and x = b, as ∫b a f(x) dx

tex: Recognise, in the case where $f(x)\le 0$ for all values of $x$ in the interval $a\le x\le b$, the area bounded by the graph of the continuous function $y=f(x)$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=a$ and $x=b$, as $\left|\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\right|$ or $-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$

text: Use definite integrals to solve problems involving the areas of regions bounded by the graph of the continuous function y = f(x), the x-axis and the lines x = a and x = b, in cases where f(x)≥0 throughout a ≤x ≤b, f(x)≤0 throughout a ≤x ≤b or where f(x) changes sign in the interval a ≤x ≤b, with or without the graph provided
tex: Use definite integrals to solve problems involving the areas of regions bounded by the graph of the continuous function $y=f(x)$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=a$ and $x=b$, in cases where $f(x)\ge 0$ throughout $a\le x\le b$, $f(x)\le 0$ throughout $a\le x\le b$ or where $f(x)$ changes sign in the interval $a\le x\le b$, with or without the graph provided

tex: Use definite integrals to solve problems involving the areas of regions bounded by the graph of the continuous function $y=f(x)$, the $y$-axis and the lines $y=a$ and $y=b$, in cases where $x\ge 0$ throughout $a\le y\le b$, $x\le 0$ throughout $a\le y\le b$ or where $x$ changes sign in the interval $a\le y\le b$ with or without the graph provided

tex: Use the fact that the graphs of $y=a^x$ and $y=\log_a x$ are reflections of each other in the line $y=x$ to solve problems involving areas between the $x$-axis or $y$-axis and a curve involving either an exponential or logarithmic function

text: Recognise and use the result, where f(x) is continuous on the interval a ≤x ≤c, ∫b a f(x)dx + ∫c b f(x)dx = ∫c a f(x)dx for all c such that a ≤b ≤c
tex: Recognise and use the result, where $f(x)$ is continuous on the interval $a\le x\le c$, $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx+\int_b^c f(x)\,dx=\int_a^c f(x)\,dx$ for all $c$ such that $a\le b\le c$

tex: Identify any values of $x$ where a function is continuous, but not differentiable, given either the equation of the function or its graph

tex: Graph the function $Q=Ae^{kt}$, where $k>0$ and $k<0$ and $A>0$ and $A<0$, with and without graphing applications, and identify any asymptotes

tex: Generate and use the formulas $\mathrm{E}(X)=\mu=\Sigma xP(x)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)=\sigma^2=\Sigma(x-\mu)^2P(x)=\Sigma x^2P(x)-\mu^2$ for the random variable $X$, where $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ is the variance and $\sigma$ is the standard deviation of the distribution

tex: Recognise that the cumulative distribution function, $F(x)$, is non-decreasing for all $x$ in its domain, and graph cumulative distribution functions, given a formula for $F(x)$, with and without graphing applications

tex: Define a probability density function (PDF), $f(x)$, for a random variable $X$ with cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ as $f(x)=F'(x)$ and recognise that $P(a<X<b)=\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$
